record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.context_brief: Stability and asymptotics of graph cocycles
record.original_question: For a graph cocycle γ=Σ_a c_a·γ_a on n vertices, are combinatorial statistics of the constituent graphs—such as diameter distributions and vertex-valency distributions—stable across the full cohomology class [γ]=[γ+d(λ)] after arbitrary coboundary changes by graphs λ on n−1 vertices? Relatedly, what is the large-n and asymptotic behavior of the dimension of graph cohomology, especially near the bi-grading ray (n, 2n−2) that is relevant for Poisson-bracket symmetries, and is there a generating function for those dimensions?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. As soon as the vertex number n is large enough, are the combinatorial properties of graphs γ_a in a cocycle γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a well defined, i.e. stable over the entire equivalence class [γ] = [γ + d(λ)] modulo arbitrary coboundaries from graphs λ on n − 1 vertices ? The properties to examine can be the distribution of diameters (over the set of graphs {γ_a} forming the cocycle γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a) and distribution of vertex valencies. • What is the large-n and asymptotic (n → ∞) behaviour of the graph cohomology dimension (primarily, on or near the ray of vertex-edge bi-gradings (n, 2n − 2), which is relevant to the Poisson bracket symmetries); are the dimensions encoded by their own generating function ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G(n,k) denote the Kontsevich graph complex of equivalence classes (under sign-respecting graph automorphisms) of finite connected oriented graphs on n vertices and k edges, equipped with the standard differential d that inserts a new vertex and sums over ways of expanding an existing vertex (so coboundaries d(λ) of graphs λ on n−1 vertices land in graphs on n vertices). A graph cocycle is a finite formal linear combination γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a (with γ_a distinct equivalence classes of graphs on n vertices) satisfying d(γ) = 0, considered modulo the equivalence relation [γ] = [γ + d(λ)].

(a) Stability of combinatorial statistics. Fix n large. For a cocycle γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a on n vertices, define the multiset-valued statistics
  • Diam(γ) = the multiset of graph diameters of the γ_a, weighted by |c_a|;
  • Val(γ) = the multiset of vertex-valency distributions of the γ_a, weighted by |c_a|.
Determine whether Diam(γ) and Val(γ) (or natural normalizations thereof) are invariants of the cohomology class [γ], i.e. whether they are preserved under all coboundary modifications γ ↦ γ + d(λ) by graph cochains λ on n−1 vertices. If not invariants, identify which features of these statistics are well-defined on cohomology classes once n is sufficiently large.

(b) Asymptotics and generating function. Let H^{n,k} denote the cohomology of this graph complex in bi-grading (n vertices, k edges). Determine the large-n asymptotic behavior of dim H^{n,k}, with emphasis on the ray k = 2n − 2 (the bi-grading relevant to symmetries of Poisson brackets). In particular, determine whether there exists a generating function F(x,y) = Σ_{n,k} dim H^{n,k} x^n y^k (or its restriction along k = 2n − 2) admitting a closed form or functional equation, and describe the growth rate of dim H^{n, 2n−2} as n → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: The dimensions of Kontsevich's graph cohomology remain an active subject of computational and theoretical research. Recent work (e.g., 11-loop computations posted in 2025) extends known dimensions but no closed-form generating function or asymptotic formula along the ray (n, 2n−2) is established. The cohomological-class invariance of combinatorial statistics such as diameter and valency distributions does not appear to be settled in the literature. The problems thus appear open.

status_evidence.title: The 11-loop graph cohomology
status_evidence.snippet: Computation of the Kontsevich graph cohomology in loop order 11, and for some degrees in higher loop order.
status_evidence.claim: Recent computations extend known dimensions of graph cohomology but full asymptotics remain unknown.

status_evidence.title: Multiple edges in M. Kontsevich's graph complexes and computations of the dimensions and Euler characteristics
status_evidence.snippet: Generating function for graded dimensions of Kontsevich's graph complexes; Euler characteristics tabulated up to loop order 30.
status_evidence.claim: Generating functions exist for Euler characteristics but not for cohomology dimensions themselves.
